newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends higher in modest trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends higher in modest trade.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar finished slightly higher on Saturday, responding to the U.S. dollar's recent weakness in overseas markets, dealers said.
The local unit ended at T$27.660 against Friday's T$27.685 close, off an intra-day high of T$27.650.
Turnover through dealers was US$135 million in the shortened Saturday session.
Despite Saturday's rise, dealers expected the Taiwan dollar to remain weak next week due to domestic political uncertainties ahead of a planned cabinet reshuffle.
"Political uncertainty will likely prompt a capital outflow," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
"There are signs that some foreign funds are flowing out of the island and more investors may consider buying the U.S. dollar," the dealer said.
Dealers expect a trading range of T$27.65-70 for next week.
